rules.title: Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) Order
rules.explanation: Simple declarative sentences follow Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) order. Changing word order can invert or break meaning.

rules.title: Verbal Aspect and Tense Suffixes
rules.explanation: Verbs do not inflect for person, number, or gender. Tense and aspect use suffixes: -lo (realis/past), -bom / -bomlo (continuous), -etlo / -det / -tanglo (perfective), -po (definite/near future), -ji (distant/dubitative future).

rules.title: Active, Stative, Equational, and Prohibitive Negation
rules.explanation: Active verbs negate by reduplicating the onset consonant(s) of the final syllable + -e (cho -> choche, dam -> damde). Existential/possessive 'do' negates with 'ave'. Equational/nominal sentences negate with 'kali'. Prohibitive commands use -ri.
rules.source_section: Stative Verbs & The Negation or Negating Process

rules.title: Yes/No (-ma) and Content (ko-) Questions
rules.explanation: Yes/no questions add sentence-final -ma. Content questions use interrogative words prefixed with ko- (kopi 'what', komat 'who', konat/kodak 'where', komantu 'when', koson 'how').

rules.title: Commands, Requests, Hortatives, and Polite -ik-
rules.explanation: Use -non/-noi for immediate commands, -tha for requests, -tu for advice, and -nang for inclusive hortatives ('let's...'). For respected elders, use honorific pronouns (-li) and insert -ik- before the verb ending.

rules.title: Postpositions Follow Nouns
rules.explanation: Spatial and relational markers follow the noun/pronoun rather than preceding it: arlo (inside), athak (on/above), arum (under), pen (by/with/from), aphan (for/to).

rules.title: Numeral Classifiers
rules.explanation: Counting uses category classifiers: -nut (1 human) / bang- (2+ humans), -jon (animals), -pak (flat objects), -pum (round objects), -pu (flowers). Numeral 'one' (i-/e-) precedes the classifier; 2+ follow it.
